resources.string: Pick the car above and the picture will show its socket.
The socket is usually under the dash on the driver\'s side, next to the steering column.
The drawing shows the typical spot, not this exact car. It can differ by year and trim.
On %1$s it\'s most often here (%2$d of %3$d models). Pick the model to be sure.

string-array.name: guide_steps
string-array.item: How to test
1. Ignition on, engine off. \"Connect\" → adapter → \"Start\".
2. Wait until \"Scanning the car…\" disappears on \"Main\". The first time takes a few minutes.
3. Start the engine, idle for 5–10 minutes.
4. Drive 20–40 minutes: city, steady 60 and 90 km/h, accelerations, one full-throttle run.
5. At idle: \"Codes\" → \"Read\", \"Info\" → \"Mode 06\".
6. Stop the engine, tap ✕ at the top, ⇪ to send the session.
Don\'t touch the phone while driving. Don\'t clear codes.

string-array.name: guide_more_steps
string-array.item: Step by step
The first connection is slow: the app is looking for the car\'s modules. It remembers them, and after that connecting takes under a minute.
Starting from a cold engine is better: you see it warm up and the idle come down.
The open tab is polled more often. While driving, keep \"Main\" or \"Fuel\" open. \"All data\" cycles through everything, so each value updates slowly there.
If something odd happens on the road (a jerk, a stumble), note the time.
After the drive, tap \"Rescan\" on \"Info\" and \"Read all modules\" on \"Codes\": new codes and test results may show up.
You can turn the screen off; recording goes on in the background.

string-array.name: guide_gm
string-array.item: GM
The first connection takes about a minute: the app looks for the modules and reads their codes.
Airbags, cluster, radio, climate and TPMS are on a separate bus (pin 1); a plain ELM327 can\'t see them.
If the engine is tuned to run open loop or without O2 sensors, the fuel trims sit at zero and the O2 readings don\'t move.

string-array.name: guide_vag
string-array.item: Volkswagen
A Polo 9N (up to about 2009) with a petrol engine is usually on K-line. Then only standard OBD is read.
The first connection takes about two minutes: the app looks for the modules and reads their part numbers and codes. On cars up to about 2012 it only finds the engine and the gearbox.
If you have time, with the car parked: \"GM scan\" → \"Find modules\", then on the engine module scan \"F100–F1FF\" or \"1000–1FFF\". It takes a while.

string-array.name: guide_toyota
string-array.item: Toyota
The RAV4 2005 doesn\'t report its VIN, so pick the car above by hand.

What\'s needed is a recording of the engine module data. Start the engine, \"GM scan\" → \"Find modules\". On \"Engine (7E0)\" tap \"$21\" (20–40 seconds), then \"Tick all with data\". Go to \"Main\" and drive for 15–20 minutes: warm-up, idle, accelerations, engine braking.
The same screen has \"Sniff bus\": 1–2 minutes with the engine running.
If the car is on K-line, connecting takes longer (up to half a minute) and only standard OBD is read.

string-array.name: guide_lada
string-array.item: Lada
The Vesta is on CAN; standard OBD is read in full.
The first connection takes about 20 seconds: the app looks for the modules and reads their part numbers and codes. It doesn\'t find ABS, airbags or the body module.

string-array.name: guide_hyundai
string-array.item: Hyundai
The Solaris is usually on CAN. If the car is from 2010 or earlier, it\'s most likely an Accent or Verna. The protocol is shown on \"Info\".

The Coupe 2003 is on K-line; the engine and the automatic transmission answer. In \"GM scan\", tap \"$21\" on each module, then \"Tick all with data\" and go for a drive. On K-line the scan takes a minute or two.
The first connection takes about 20 seconds: the app looks for the modules and reads their part numbers and codes. It doesn\'t find ABS, airbags or body modules.

string-array.name: guide_safety
string-array.item: Safety
The app only reads. One button can change something in the car, \"Clear\" on \"Codes\", and it asks first.
Clearing erases not only the codes but also the readiness monitors and the freeze frame. The codes themselves are already saved in the session by then.
Run the scans in \"GM scan\" and the bus sniffing while parked: live data isn\'t read while they run.

string-array.name: guide_files
string-array.item: What\'s in a session
raw.log — the whole exchange with the adapter.
data.csv — all values over time.
report.txt — summary: adapter, VIN, modules, codes, tests.
scan.csv and bus.csv — module scans and bus sniffing.
sensors.csv — phone accelerometer and gyroscope. Without an adapter: \"Phone sensors\" on \"Connect\", then \"Start\".
